text: To get home, Apollo thirteen had to go all the way around the Moon first.
Their main engine sat in the damaged service module, too risky to fire. So they borrowed the Moon's gravity instead.
A short burn of the lunar module's landing engine put them on a path that loops around the Moon, and falls back toward Earth.
Behind the Moon, they were farther from Earth than any humans had ever been.
Another burn sped them up, and about four days after the explosion, they splashed down safely.
